Prevention: Increase plant spacing (25x25 cm) (depending on variety and soil to increase aeration and reduce humidity).
Field sanitation such as removing weed hosts, rice straws, ratoons, and volunteer seedlings is important to avoid infection caused by this disease.
Draining the field during severe flooding.
Apply fertilizer in balance ratio (avoid overdosing nitrogen).
Plough stalk after harvesting to minimize the initial inoculum at the beginning of the season.
Monitoring: Scouting 3 times per week especially when the weather is cold.
Look for narrow, dark-greenish water-soaked interveinal streaks on inter-veins from tillering to booting stage.
Under humid conditions, yellow droplets of bacterial ooze, which contain masses of bacterial cells
Direct Control: Remove infested plants and burn or use for composting.
When yield is affected, a copper- based fungicide applied at heading stage can be effective in controlling the disease.
Restrictions: There is no chemical control for bacterial diseases on rice.
